# Chapter 23

Paranoid Operating System Methodology for Anonymous and Secure Web Browsing

*   Nuno Ricardo Mateus-Coelho  
    [![Orcid Image](i/orcid.svg)https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5517-9181](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5517-9181)  
    Universidade de Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro, Portugal
*   Benjamim Ribeiro Fonseca  
    Universidade de Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro, Portugal
*   António Vieira Castro  
    Instituto Superior de Engenharia do Porto, Portugal

ABSTRACT

It has recently been discovered that large companies and nations “observe” their customers and citizens, disregarding any remaining moral and technological lines, being able to listen to telephone conversations and monitoring communications through powerful monitoring and surveillance programs. Elsewhere on the planet, nations in turmoil or wrapped in a cloak of censorship persecute their citizens, controlling them by denying them access to the free web without the threat of repercussions that threatens their dignity. To support the present research, an analysis of platforms that allow anonymous and secure browsing and a study of technologies and programs with potential privacy breach and computer intrusion were performed. The main objective of this work was to analyse the computer monitoring and surveillance technologies, identifying the available tools, trying to find potential solutions, developing and providing a methodology that enhances any desktop, server, or mobile operating system, with characteristics that combat the exposed in this summary.

INTRODUCTION

According to David Whitley (Whitley, 2009) human communication goes back to the earliest history records, approximately thirty to forty thousand years ago. Initially, they were symbols used for the passage of knowledge, e.g., to identify behaviours or mundane aspects to the surroundings and territories, dangers or just leisure. It was about 9.000 years ago that man began the arduous task of writing words with meaning and with the intention of passing or retaining knowledge the future generations. The organized writing system with semantic content also appeared approximately 6.000 years ago. From then onwards, the great technological evolutions that followed were always accompanied by the registration of activities and their planning, in written form in every means possible (Whitley, 2009). The evolution was such that, nowadays, writing is mostly done digitally by means of multimedia tools and data entry in computers, being atomically spread by technological means by millions and millions of people across continents. According to Mark Zuckerberg (Zuckerberg, 2015), in 2015, on 8 September, 1 in 7 humans were linked at the same time to Facebook (digital social network) and more was to be expected in the future, aiming to double that amount by the end of 2020, an astronomical deed from the time the man made engravings in cave walls.

We live in a time when society is challenged by sudden change with social, political, economic and high environmental costs. This volatility implies strong consequences for the (in) security of societies and organizations. The speed at which events happen, new technological offers, new trends, products, problems and solutions rises, create a disruption that already has today, and despite the efforts of those who regulate, an impact virtually impossible to contain or hide. The research and massive use of information and social sharing of it, was created by the advent Web 2.0 or 2^(nd) generation Web, term introduced by Tim O'Reilly (O'Reilly, 2009), which associated with the new generation Web 3.0, characterized by the semantic Web, a term introduced by John Markoff (Murugesan, 2010), (Priya et al., 2019), created an unique digital phenomena, comparable only to the human ecological footprint. The digital footprint implies that everything that is shared and exposed on the Web, to be stored somewhere in it, allowing third parties to access and save this information in computational clusters with estimated useful life impossible to calculate, thus being accessible to others for many, many generations.

By relying on Cloud platforms (data storage in virtualized computing environments) and publishing personal information on social networks, individuals opened the door to cybercrime (crimes committed using information technologies) which for years targeted only corporations. Being a living entity, in the broadest sense of the sentence, globalization, this network made up of people and machines, is also a source of misinformation directed to nations that compete with each other, where, whom first holds the validated information has in fact, leadership (Zarghoon et al., 2017), and to achieve this, whether economic or strategic, mechanisms are created that advocate computer insecurity through violation, decoding, modification and interception of data with the objective of retaining private information for their own benefit.

Computer security is constantly being tested. According to Paulo Santos (Santos et al., 2008) from computer pirates commonly known as hackers to government intelligence agencies, everyone wants a piece of this El Dorado, being just a matter of ego or economic benefits and strategic advantage in the game of international politics. Also, computer systems connected using a network and, above all, the wide network that is the Web, are daily used to store and manipulate information by millions of people and organizations. According to Herman Walker (Walker, 2009) schools, universities, medical offices, students, teachers, medical staff or any indigent, all of them exchange information through computer networks; Now, it is safe to say that information is in circulation, so it is critical that this information is kept in security.

As written above, computer security is a key element in this work and will be given relevant correspondence to the issues, with specific detail and focus on the programs and mechanisms that allow to track, verify, triangulate and store information about users when they use the Web. How can user security be reinforced respecting their need for transparency? How can the overall security be upheld, and Web insecurity be combated?

The authors identified how to overcome major technical barriers imposed by Internet service providers around the world, by analysing how to access the deep web proxy system. The end result of the analysis of these systems is the creation of a methodology with a set of ground rules and mechanisms applicable to any type operating system, capable of deployment in a desktop, server or mobile device, replicating the same security principals, thus demonstrating that the methodology is practical and executable in different environments, running from the memory, hard drive or as a paranoid mode in an operating system, equal to a debug or safe mode thus obtaining a consolidated answer to the questions and challenges that impose insecurity, while using common operative systems. In this research, two prototypes were developed, one as Live Image (virtual operating system that works from the memory of its host), and the other, the one that will serve as an example for an installation scenario; a mobile distribution that will be used to prove that the methodology is cross platform and usable in an installed environment. The objective is to show that any kind of operating system, given the chance of setting accordingly, can be prepared to use the Web anonymously. Part of the information provided in this research is the result of an analysis to the computer underworld via the Tor (The Onion Router) network or anonymity network, collected in conversations for months on end for the past 4 years. Here, it was possible to gather information and confer with whom is usually 100% dedicated to this type of initiatives.

This research aims to know the technologies that threatens everyone and the main alternatives that exist to circumvent and deceive them. The overall goal is to provide any given operating system various anonymous and secure browsing solutions that will allow less able users to autonomously configure a prototype on their systems. The solution, in the form of the referred prototypes, that in an optimum way should run from the memory only, should be deployed on a computer and will allow the safe and anonymous Web browsing. It will contain and allow the following:

*   • Browse the Web anonymously without leaking or revealing the geographical position or IP of origin, recurring to filters that prevent brute force over the user;
*   • Communicate securely through an encrypted secure chat system, without the need to establish a VPN channel across the Web;
*   • Bypass traffic blocking systems, firewalls and censorship mechanisms, and do it so without violating any law;
*   • Do not leave a trace of use on the computer of if so, one that cannot be diverted from the user, or provide the geographical location of the user and what they do or have done on the Web;
*   • High-level encryption technology, natively available, easy and simple to install if needed;
*   • Mechanism that prevent data collection from any entity beside the user.

The prototypes also contain a mix of solutions that allow its users to get the best of both worlds when it comes to computer security:

*   • Computer security and secure Web browsing through anonymity;
*   • Computer security through offensive mechanisms;
*   • Computer security using isolation techniques;
*   • Secure and isolated tools for daily use;
*   • The secure use of the Web recurring to a secure proxy chain, the Tor network or the I2P Network.

BACKGROUND

Computer security is increasingly a social problem and a technical problem. Technical problem because the variety of systems, standards, architectures, methodologies such as ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library), COBIT (Control Objectives for Information and Related Technology)¹, TOGAF (The Open Group Architecture Framework)², SOA (Software Oriented Architecture)³, versions of operating systems, hardware and their requirements, software requirements, among many examples, make the task of implementing security measures and norms, risk mitigation circuits and drafting of computer director plans that anticipate and respond to unexpected issues, an immensely complex task, thus, culminating in the impossibility of creation or full coverage of effective security policies. Just add to the equation the connection to distributed systems that is now the Web, to really become an almost impossible task (Lopez et al., 2015).

A social problem, for non-technical users of these systems lack to have a sense of the needs or notice any safety issues. For these, according to Brian Shea (Shea, 2002), all the effort and systems behind the screen are transparent, and not contribute with higher attention to detail because they feel safe having antivirus software and a firewall sending graphic alerts throughout GUI (Graphic User Interface), to the computer technicians who implement secure measures and support them in the day-to-day difficulties in organizations.

Also, on a daily basis, applications are developed aiming to exploit and misdirect the general public or system administrators, and as countermeasures, every day reputed companies develop and launch applications to the market to enable them to avoid mechanisms that insist on violating computer privacy, e.g., through the sharing of resources like the random access memory. (Ghafari et al., 2017).

Throughout the years, computer solutions were created aiming to maintain information security and the users of this information. Entities such as Symantec (software and computer security company) launch updates to their antivirus programs daily in an attempt to respond to the threats created. Companies such as Microsoft create updates and patches that they make available regularly to correct errors and vulnerabilities in the software they develop and sell. Companies such as CISCO⁴ develop network appliances (equipment) that are subject to adjustments, with other features that are not adjustable in order to standardize concepts of security and defence mechanisms (Shelly & Campbell, 2012). Nevertheless, this outlook and these measures are no more than reactive to daily challenges and regrettably, not preventive.

According to Paulo Santos (Santos et al., 2008), for prevention, there are complex security policies and mechanisms that are established and fully accepted by entities that develop equipment and software but are not always implemented by end users. According to the same author, security policies define the focus of security and what security should ensure. Mechanisms are the technology that enables the implementation of security policies. A security domain consists of a universe of resources (machines and networks) and people subject to the same security policies. These aim at guaranteeing the confidentiality of private information, aiming at the protection of critical information, targeting at the continuity of the operation or provision of services, pointing at confidence in correcting system operation, aiming at proof of correction or authorship in the exchange of information, and forcing, among many other guarantees, the ability to audit past actions.

As with everything else in life, there will always exist risks because it is impossible to assure that a certain system is 100% secure or protected against threats. For risk management within the information security, the society makes efforts and conventions that bring together methods designed to reduce the risk of intrusion. These norms or standards are generally applicable to societies and ultimately to citizens, because it is the societies that will implement them for citizens to use them. Norms, as the Standard ISO (International Organization for Standardization) / IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission) 27001 (Calder & Watking, 2015), provide appropriate approaches for risk management systems. This standard provides a framework of best practices for the management of information security and IT infrastructures.

For all this, it is clear that computer security and the need for mechanisms that effectively protect users are the order of the day. The Web carries public and private information, making it difficult to separate the two, and time is a constant in constant movement, insuring factual technological evolution.

THE PROBLEM

According to Symantec, in the Insecurity of Internet of Things Report, at the end 2019 it is estimated that approximately 5.9 billion devices will be connected to the Web (Barcena & Wueest, 2019). Many of these will be devices that have insufficient active and passive security mechanisms. Such devices that people use massively on a daily basis and as routine, are laptops, smartwatches, health bands and bracelets, mobile phones, tablets and smartphones, many Linux based, extremely insecure and collectors of sensible information. Regardless of this panorama, everyday millions and millions of users share information and data through these devices. It is through this type of equipment that the younger generations, and not only, communicate with each other, to the point that they already make video and voice calls over the Internet protocol, also known as Voice Over IP (VoIP) or Voice over Internet Protocol, to save communication costs, recurring to platforms that announce at their launching phase to be secure and safe, and afterwards security leaks proved otherwise e.g., WhatsApp, (Lakshmanan, 2019), (Rösler et al., 2018).

Currently organizations have ceased to be the direct target of those dedicated to theft and misuse of information, the average user has become a target due to the amount of information shared online, without the notion of his digital footprint. There are also attacks on systems that provide services, such as Web servers that store information about users, as was the case of the alleged attack on the EuroMillions online platform, reported by the website pplware.sapo.pt in May 2015 (Pplware, 2015). The form of the attack has not been revealed and the type of exposed data could be used for future attacks. The elements exposed consisted of username, hash, MD5 (Message Digest 5), salt, email addresses and birthdays. MD5 generates 128bit hash codes in length and was developed by Ron Rivest of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1991 and is specified in RFC 1321, (Barret, 2005). Given that the algorithm has several weaknesses already documented, (Zúquete, 2014), its use is discouraged. However, it was allegedly in use when the alleged attack occurred, and considering that this platform record gambling pay-out data, credit card information, account banking information and other private information, system administration and programmers could and should have foreseen the problem. As it can be concluded, human error prevails in many security issues and breaches because it is based on the assumptions that certain attacks do not occur in a specific geographic location or area, in this case Portugal. As example, such attacks are not common in Portugal, but the Web is global and the servers, websites, repositories of data, among others, are available literally from every point of the planet, requiring only an internet connection to access them (Oriyano, 2016).

The year 2013 was rich in revealing events and activities of North American security entities. According to revelations from security tech guru, Julien Assange (Assange, 2013) on Wikileaks (online platform for sharing information), secure Web browsing does not exist and even the location of users is not safeguarded. According to him, several countries can access user data and extract relevant information. Failure to use secure passwords, encrypted operating systems, firewall, unlicensed software, use of software recurring to cracks’ (programs designed to overcome the requirement of legitimate license) and other mechanisms, facilitate the work of these harmful entities (Boavida et al., 2013).

The possible lack of user knowledge of technical and security issues has led to 220.000 Apple device owners becoming vulnerable, and with them, Apple's iCloud (cloud storage platform) systems (Hyslip, 2014). Anyone who uses Cydia-style programs to buy prohibited applications on branded equipment may end up buying applications that allow such attacks. It is not known concretely which vulnerability was used, but the suspicions fall on a backdoor in jailbreak methods (jailbreak method, freeing a device from Apple control). This attack has had great notoriety, being known as the case of celebrity photographs.

Initially under attack with Phishing technics, the average user is now followed carefully when browsing through various websites. Users are closely followed by cookies that aim to pass information of browsing habits for advertisement companies that will present to them commercial content in other Web pages e.g., the advertising of services and products connected to their taste. It is also through cookies that various websites store users' session information (names and passwords), exposing them to attacks that capture confidential information. This transmission of information through cookies makes navigation much simpler, creating a false sense of knowledge and mastery of technologies, which in turn leads to carelessness and, ultimately, information theft in the best of scenarios (Nirmal et al., 2018).

Operating systems control all environment, technically speaking, non the less, attacks on isolated organizational computer systems, systems that provide services, attacks or attempts to control the ordinary users, exist and are widely known. The starting point is, in the vast majority of cases, carelessness in security methods, insecure and non-up-to-date operating systems, lack of knowledge in how to use complex security systems or ignorance of existence of simple security programs to use. There are countries that, due to their political characteristics, employ tight control over access to web-based content. According to (Deibert et al., 2008), countries like North Korea, that limit access to technology, e.g., only some people may have access to devices that allow them to access the Web, and those who have them still have to go through a barrier imposed by ISP’s (Internet Service Providers), such as Vodafone in Portugal, which make it impossible for them to view content from certain websites, countries, religions, etc.

The most notorious case of the previous scenario is placed in another Asian country and called the Great Firewall of China, also known as the Golden Shield Project, developed by the military computer division of the People's Republic of China (Qinglian, 2006). This advanced firewall, automatically and through the analysis of all incoming and outgoing traffic, realizes whether that information should or not be censored. Overcoming this barrier is complex and extremely insecure due to the many steps and operations required, e.g., the use of a Web proxy. To trust proxy systems is to trust all the information forwarded and received through that channel, to those who manage it.

If the CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the heart of a given system, the operating system is the brain behind everything. Literally everything that runs on electronical equipment require an operating system of some kind. In the past operating systems where the main focus and attractions of the computer history, feud of mighty technological and legal wars between the Cupertino and Redmond giants, and epic scripts to may famous movies and cinema tales. Despite the cinematic mist something cannot be denied. In the mid 80’s the operating systems were the flag of all companies and if we have technology as we have it now, it is set upon systems like Linux, Windows.

This panorama created the world as we know it now, connected, available, nice and beautiful, transparent and easy to use, although not without a great cost to the end user, the security. Operating systems nowadays are designed to interconnect devices and create at a first glance an ecosystem between equipment of the same brand, and later in the interconnectivity between ecosystems of different companies. These work best if connect to payed systems and services of a given vendor and connect better or smoothly if a specific network technology is set to use. In some cases, even the backup systems have a specific language to speak with specific operating systems. This is achievable using specific standards, same vendor technology, and consortiums among companies. All of this is possible but only recurring to transparency of use, and this means creating simple systems, in a type of dummy proof environment. This is simply observable just by watching how applications are installed and the type of data they collect. Transparency can even be observed in cluster or service servers, with despite the ease of use, can create a danger road down the line (Goscinski et al., 2002).

Finally, quite recently, in 2018, Facebook was observed selling 87 million users’ information and data, involving them in a great scandal called Cambridge Analytica. In 2017 the Botnet Mirai it hard in the IoT industry, piggy hopping millions of devices across the globe and spreading rapidly, blocking everting in the way, from hospitals to universities, any operating system without proper attention was infected and cripple, joining a rapidly growing network that spread computer insecurity across the Web (Antonakakis et al., 2017).

THE PROMINET THREATS

According to Paul O'Day in the Journal of Education of Pacific University (O'Day, 2013), the North American government has been monitoring the Web since its appearance. Its military genesis places government institutions in a privileged place in relation to the others. What was not initially expected when Internet became a global tool e.g., total freedom of communication, is now difficult to control without resource to complex surveillance tools, and academic and scientific brains daily move the technical chess in a constant escape-pursuit game. Brilliant minds like Steve Wozniak, Bill Gates, Tim Berners Lee, James Gosling, Linus Torvalds, Richard Stallman, Artur C. Clarke, Ted Shirley, Martha Lane Fox and many others, are constantly researching and influencing the world and the new generations, in a strife between freedom, quality software, and mass control, thus effectively creating great difficulties for those who advocate the violation of privacy and information deft.

The most effective way to compromise security is to listen and inject the ISP (Internet Service Provider), before the data reaches the destination system. If the communications and connections are not encrypted, or in some cases even if they are, it is possible to discover the user location, message content, unique information about the computer and above all, with the connection details and crossings of data, to know who specifically the user is (Locati, 2015).

Also, it cannot be forgotten or denied that many data circulating is encrypted, but is also known and non-deniable the promiscuity among the large technology companies such as Facebook and Google, and their ability to circumvent the security impositions, namely complex techniques such as encryption (Nowakowsk, 2015).

Still according to Tomas Nowakowsk (Nowakowsk, 2015), until recently, it was not known that the NSA was spying on internet users at national and international level. Through the press NSA advertised that the platforms they own does not violate anyone’s privacy, something that Edward Snowden denied categorically with documental support in the form of 58.000 classified and secret documents, alerting the world to this grim reality (Landau, 2014). He used daily newspapers and the Wikileaks Website to share this information, becoming a wanted person around the world and living in Russia to avoid the justice of the United States, where he would surely be imprisoned perpetually or sentenced to death for treason.

Above the programs and the entities, there are the always unwanted friend. Individuals who dedicate themselves to exploiting information systems with various types of intents, some innocuous, others not so much, and Eduard Snowden was firstly labelled one of these individuals by United States Authorities. There is an extensive class of professionals in this field, as the reader will observe later in this chapter.

1\. Prism

Confirming the initial suspicions Mark Klein, a former AT & T telecom engineer, (Kravets, 2013), (Lind, 2015), (Bamford, 2013), about the existence of a program that monitored and analysed telephone communications directly in telecommunications companies, it was acknowledged that the NSA does so through a surveillance technological program called Prism (Savage, 2013). This was born in 2007 under the Protect America Act, under the aegis of the President of the United States of America at the time. The existence of Prism has been recognised by the U.S. government since the cabinet of Freedom of Information Office initiated the inquiries (White House, 2013).

According to Elliot Cohen (Cohen, 2015) and Bruce Schneider (Schneider, 2015), Prism is a tool that allows to circumvent complex encryption, one of the greatest difficulties of those who dedicate themselves to study and analyse the traffic that circulates in packages. As more and more encryption methods are used, the DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) technique becomes obsolete. The DPI consists of filtering the content and header of a data packet in transit through the Web. In other words, it allows to know who sent it, who received it, and what is the content of a given data packet. If this data circulates encrypted, it does not mean that the DPI is useless, it just means that additional tools will be needed.

2\. Muscular

It was the year 2013 and there was still no research or understood well the intricacies and broad spectrum of the Prism application, when the MUSCULAR was also exposed. This is a joint surveillance effort between the United States and the United Kingdom through the NSA agencies and their English counterpart, GCHQ (Government Communications Headquarters). Also known by its code name DS-200B, it aims to successfully invade the information processing centres of Google and Yahoo, reaching and retrieving data that is stored on their computer nodes, and from the Google Enterprise Cloud (Google Cloud).

Of origin identical to the Prism, this collects immensely more computer data, because it is not limited by the same judicial rules that prevail in the United States mainland (Jalalzai, 2017).

Its concrete location is in the UK and came to the public through NSA systems analyst Edward Snowden in April 2013, and later, according to Barton Gellman and DeLong (Gellman & DeLong, 2013) of the Washington Post newspaper, confirmed by officers who serve in Naval War College.

According to Elliot Cohen (Cohen, 2015), the Muscular collects direct data that will feed the Prism databases, among others, and allow to uncover the location of a given user, as well as the online habits.

3\. Golden Shield and Similar Solutions

According to Neil Huges (Huges, 2016), technological growth and the evolution of financial markets based on technologies are antagonistic to societies that control the freedom of expression of their citizens. According to the same author, China has a communist dictatorial regime, established more than 50 years ago. This regime, which advocates the Iron Bowl system, e.g., nothing will fail the people and all the goods needed for survival are guaranteed, including lifetime work, controls sagaciously all sorts of external information that reaches to the people. These types of regimes are historically doomed to failure or misery, as can be seen now in North Korea and some countries from the former Soviet Union.

Still according to the same author, with the growth of financial markets, China decided to enter the leading economic game and began mass production of almost everything that the world consumes, establishing itself in 2017 as the second largest productive market in the world, behind only the United States of America. By wanting to maximize profits (capitalist inverse management of communism), China decided that it would open the doors of business to its population, which implies being able to communicate with the world to avoid miss out opportunities. This opening led to the fact that the Web was within reach of all the Chinese citizens and especially to the opposition that made it possible to pass information on Western developments, and the comfort of most of its pollutions. To circumvent this issue, the Ministry of Public Security launched the Golden Shield Project. An advance stat of the art system, consisting in one of the most sophisticated data packet verification firewalls in the world, placed at the entrance and exit of China’s Web connection.

According to Sarosh Kuruvilla, (Kuruvilla et al., 2011), after the arrival of the Internet, the Chinese government in 1997 placed in action the first control measures, issuing regulations over the use, and the first appropriate penalties to misuse. In 1998, the Communist Party, with fear of losing control of the country, gave instructions to elaborate a network capable of controlling all Web traffic going in and out of China, and named the Great Firewall of China, employing more than 45.000 police officers being a complex network of proxy servers that prevent Chinese IP from coming out, by anything else than one of the six Chinese gateways (at the time).

4\. Cambridge Analytica and Similar Actions

According to David Carroll (The Great Hack, 2019), associate professor at Parson School, the accuracy of advertising sent to users of social networks is remarkable. When he was referring to social networks, he was referring to Facebook. This fact shows that the data collected will be of an incalculable magnitude because the amount of detail in advertising sent to users is so accurate that it can only come from an extensive and complex prediction algorithm. The source of information collection is wider than just voluntary collection via social networks, as part of its sources are more technological and closer to the user’s devices, namely the collection by intermediate of smartphones and other equipment. These have mechanisms such as microphones and geo-location collectors, which allow entities like Facebook to perceive the concrete location of users by making a cross-reference with their services and inputs provided, e.g., likes, shares etc.

5\. Operative Systems and Third-Party Applications for Mobile

Security is something ardours to obtain and it comes as a daily task. According to Kai Qian, (Qian et al., 2018), security threats in the mobile segment grow exponentially mainly because of programming error, planed backdoor and the commercial intent surrounding users, being the data collection business a source of data misleading and insecurity.

Most applications in Play Store⁵ and App Store⁶ require non-needed sources of data from the user equipment, e.g., access to the image portfolio, SMS content, microphone activation, access to stored conversation or recordings, smartphone geo-location via GPS module, Web location when using the internet and other sensors of a given device with only one intent, collect, store and sell this information (Han et al., 2015), as it was possible to observe in the previous point with Cambridge Analytica.

According to Hongmu Han (Han et al., 2015), Android is a complex and extensive software and only few users can dominate and configure properly this operating system, and this operating system is always collecting data from the user to send to Googles knowledge databases. This allows Google to refine methods to target more services to their Android users.

According to Paloalto’s researcher Cong Zheng & Tongbo Luo (Zheng & Luo, 2016) the way data is misled in smartphones is recurring to storage access and data capture via application, legitimate or viruses one’s.

6\. Hacker and Crackers

Threats are not only of governmental origin or of more or less secret societies. It is also a harmful and profitable criminal activity, a call of attention to the computer problems existing on platforms or systems, a source of information that allows third parties to obtain a revealing position in the use of this information and many other activities. According to Eric Raymond (Raymond, 1997), and according to Moore (Moore, 2015), there is a group of people who, using the high computer skills they possess, with very specific objectives, are dedicated to developing their capacities to exploit, modify or access systems that they do not own.

THE METHODOLOGY

The POSMASWEB – Paranoid Operating System Methodology for Anonymous & Secure Web Browsing consist in the application of a strict set of rules. These rules were applied to two prototypes in order to demonstrate the methodology viability. The methods and technologies related to the prototype development were analysed and assorted, e.g., the base operating systems, the analysis of development of ground solutions and the selection of the modules that allow a concrete answer the problem studied and listed in the previous points.

The proposed methodology uses some techniques that are commonly available in critical systems such as the ones available in nuclear power stations, commonly known as Air Gap systems and techniques, recommended by Bruce Schneider (Blunden & Cheung, 2014), a recognised expert in cryptography and writer of computer sciences books on the computer security themes and also a professor at Harvard University. The prototypes are not Air Gap systems but able to be set as such.

The methodology establishes that there will not be set as enabled, specific tools that are not essential to the use of safe navigation, that said, the prototypes are absent of such tools. Such tools if available will allow third parties to exploit them via the Web, thus leading to the discovery of the equipment and evidently, the user.

As a general objective, this methodology intents to be a source of information and awareness of a real and even somewhat frightening panorama that currently takes advantage of the vast complex resources and contradictory information.

1\. Prototype Architectures

The two prototypes are based in the following types of architecture:

*   • x86/64 - As a system that can be run virtually from a machine's memory, thus overcoming any hardware constraints, and that can be used on any type digital support or electronic media e.g., USB stick, memory card or DVD;
*   • RISC/ARM - As a second prototype in a mobile installable version, which can be installed on any device compatible with the selected technology, in this case Android.

In the following points, the desktop and mobile version conceptual models are available, as well as brief points in their development, security methods, application selection, communication methods, event management, core hardening, resources, among other key factors. In figure nº. 1 and figure nº.2 is displayed the conceptual models of each prototype.

The entire research consisted on a broad analysis of computer security, threats, solutions and the respective development of a concrete prototype containing the latest technologies to allow the user to surf the Web securely, anonymously, without revealing the user geographical and physical location among other specific information. It is important to keep in mind that a mobile device commonly possesses more private information than a computer, hence it is handier to the user.

Subsequently, was submitted to functional and quality tests, as well as feasibility and safety tests to a group of participants who later answered a questionnaire, in order to assist in the validation of the prototype. To achieve the objective, the following measures were applied:

*   • Add new applications that ensure security;
*   • Ass new applications that ensure privacy;
*   • Block the execution of JavaScript code by default;
*   • Harden the kernel and isolate applications;
*   • Redirect all IP traffic through an encrypted virtual tunnel to a network that ensures security, privacy and anonymity:
*   • Removal of GPS functionality;
*   • Removal of native applications using insecure communication protocols;
*   • Survey and update access permissions of native applications.

According to Walter Funny and Jörg Sauerbrey (Funny & Sauerbrey, 2013) totally secure systems are an otopy, thus, no system can claim to be 100% secure guaranteeing full privacy and anonymity. It is expected that measures applied to the prototype can demonstrate the best available techniques and practices for browse the Web safely, leaving no trace or the possibility of locating and detecting the communications content between the prototype and the web.

2.1 Problems to Overcome

The first vulnerabilities exploited in mobile phones date back to the 1980’s shortly after their emergence. There were few threats at the time, due to the limited functionality of the equipment. They were mainly concentrated on the services that operators provided:

*   • Caller ID - Identification of intervenient in phone call;
*   • Calls - Applications that performs calls and accesses phone records;
*   • Messages - Applications that sends messages and accesses phone records;
*   • Voicemail \- Applications that accesses recorded messages and accesses phone records;

Nowadays, as a result of the evolution of characteristics and the similarity of features of a smartphone and a computer, vulnerabilities are concentrated in the device. In the first quarter of 2017, 1.5 million security incidents involving smartphones were detected (Davis & Samani, 2019).

Most security and privacy breaches come from apps available on the Google Play Store, which are not controlled by their analysts and distribute unsecure content to users. Hundreds of new applications are added every day without any prior control and Google's positioning has been based on a reactive, rather than preventive approach which according to the above publication, more than half of the security applications available on Google Play Store, mostly antivirus application, have no practical effect or are ineffective (AV- Comparatives, 2018) or are in fact bait for the unsuspecting user.

Some applications such as Facebook, have access to sensitive user data, e.g., call log and SMS message content (Gallagher, 2018). In the paper “Won’t Somebody Think of the Children” it is indicated that 3300 applications are available on the Google Play Store targeting kids, sharing data on user behaviour without their consent (Reyes et al., 2018). Based on a study by security company MalwareBytes, hundreds of applications were found, mostly games, that misled the user into thinking that is was playing and when is generating crypto currency (Segura, 2018).

2.2 Methodology Configurations

According to the Android Open Source Project (Android Open Source Project, n.d), the Android operating system is developed and tested by Google on the Ubuntu operating system and there is no official development support for any other platform.

Every Android’s version is directly related to an Ubuntu distribution due to the fact of specifically installed packages, e.g., the GCC compiler and the libraries needed for compilation. Both the Mobile and Desktop prototypes are based in an Ubuntu distribution, the Ubuntu 12.04 Precise Pangolin for the mobile and the Ubuntu 14.04 LTS - Trusty Tahr. The mobile prototype operating system version will be the same as the lab’s Samsung Smartphone version, the 2.3.6 with the codenamed Gingerbread. A more recent Android version was considered but discarded after a lab trial that took 12 hours to compile and ended with nearly 60Gb of image size.

For the development of the mobile prototype, several technologies were tested to verify their harmony, in order to ensure secure communications and reliable applications. Several original tools where removed due to their insecurity or promiscuous leak or sharing of information. The following list demonstrates the resources removed from the prototype and the reason for that action:

*   • Email - Storages in the mobile private information and data that is shared without the user knowledge. Recurs to SMTP which sends traffic in plain text. This prototype requires the use of webmail in a secure browser;
*   • Launcher2 - This is an Android default GUI. Was removed due to the uncertainty of data leakage;
*   • Native Web browser - Collects users browsing history, forms content, usernames and passwords, cookies storage, temporary info storage, enables insecure protocols and JavaScript usage;
*   • Play Store - No app store is included in the prototype hence the uncertainty of software providers in these types of stores;
*   • QuickSearchBox - This app was removed as its sole purpose is to conduct searches on the Google service unsafe and compromising user privacy.

The following resources were included:

*   • Nemus GUI - Open Source user interface that requires low memory usage, without offering extra features that can be diverted;
*   • The Orweb - Secure Web browser that prevents leakage of information and use of java scripts;
*   • The Orbot - Connects to the Tor Network through the SOCKS5 protocol through port 9050;
*   • Tor Network - A secure technology that enables three node circuits with three layers of encryption security;
*   • Ubuntu 12.04 LTS - This is the Precise Pangolin operating system, a reliable and solid Linux Ubuntu distribution.

The prototype developed is a stable tool, similar graphically to many other operating systems, but with its own identity, the methodology.

In this stage, the comparison was conducted to validate the prototype effectiveness regarding those specific issues and recurring to the laboratory Wireshark tool, to the prototype emulation in a virtual machine with the PID 9950; emulator and operating in the tcp.port 5554 and tcp.port 5555.

3\. Desktop Prototype

In order to confirm the methodology to desktop solutions, the desktop prototype must differ from the other examples available in the market, as e.g., prevent it from being installed on a physical drive. The main purpose of this prototype was/is to run from the computer's RAM. The full objective is to achieve the same results obtained with the mobile prototype.

It is intended that it can be used efficiently, being in its maximum amplitude an operating system like many others in terms of productivity characteristics, run securely and promoting user safety and anonymity toward the user physical location.

The desktop prototype does not assume multiple solutions for the same need and doesn’t include any “office” software, such as LibreOffice.⁷

However, it is required that this and other software to the users liking, might be safely downloaded from the Ubuntu’s Software Center (available). Whenever the prototype is closed, its contents will be irreversibly discarded. The system should work independently of any hardware installed and should be fully functional on any computer. Unlike Windows, which needs to maintain the hardware-based architecture to function (Carpenter, 2012) the prototype must operate without limits and with acceptable performance regardless of the architecture and virtual machine as it is possible to observe in the following point, the Conceptual Model.

In the following image it is presented the conceptual diagram of the desktop prototype and the two possible methods of use, Web download for direct use in virtual machine, or direct use by USB or CD / DVD drive:

| Figure 3. Desktop prototype conceptual diagram |

| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch023.f03](i/ch023.f03.png) |

In the following point is presented the detailed description of the diagram’s workflow according to each specific scenario:

*   • Option 1 - Boot from CD/DVD: The prototype starts, the user chooses the Live mode boot option; after loading the hardware drivers, the prototype behaves as if it were installed on the computer hard disk; to turn off, simply choose this option and wait for the message prompting the user to remove the CD/DVD from the CD/DVD drive;
*   • Option 2 - Use from a virtual machine: The user must download the .iso file from the appropriate repository (https://bit.ly/2NlCfTe) into the host, or to a USB stick; boot the virtual machine by selecting the installation option from an .iso image; the system recognizes the image content and automatically adjusts the technical settings. In the event that this does not happen, user needs to choose from the list of options the example Ubuntu 32Bits, with 1Gb of Ram and 20Gb of hard disk. These options are sufficient and common to commercial virtualization software (VMware, VirtualBox) for Windows, MacOS and Linux. After the previous steps, inside the virtual machine the prototype will be available. To terminate the prototype, user can shut down and wait for the confirmation message from the virtual machine, or can pause it, which will suspend the prototype. For security reasons, it is advisable to run it on a virtual machine installed on an operating system (Windows, MacOS or Linux).

3.1 Problems to Overcome

As pointed out earlier, the persistent problem is non-privacy when using the web. From operating systems to applications that share information with third parties, there are also entities that are dedicated to capturing, storing data, collecting the location of internet users, spying on their habits and conversations. Also, is considered problematic the existence of large firewalls coordinated by government entities, that deny free access to websites and other Web resources.

There are also rules imposed by the communications regulators, such as Anacom (in Portugal), which by legal directive make it impossible to access torrent file sharing websites such as Piratebay⁸.

One of the biggest problems with using information technologies is hackers obsessively looking for Web vulnerabilities and a means of making money at the expense of unwary people and businesses. As discussed earlier in this research thesis, the extensive number of attacks and intrusion mechanisms puts the most common systems at the forefront, something the methodology and the desktop prototype intends to circumvent, as it is in its genesis a system that forgets all user actions after being rebooted.

The developed desktop prototype allows, recurring to the use of diversified technology, ability to overcome the limits described as well as being a safe solution against the vulnerabilities of everyday use of the web, and currently (in February 2019), being a unique solution because it will use a double circuit inside the Tor Network, encapsulating information within three encrypted layers and three additional ones.

3.2 Methodology Configurations

There are several operating system options available for everyday use. Practically, if the decision is to use Linux as operating system, the list of systems created by people and organizations is endless. Ensuring that these versions are and remain properly secured a is a potentially difficult and exhaustive task and also the objective of the propose methodology. Nevertheless, similar products already exist, as can be seen in this document in the state-of-the-art chapter.

After careful analysis, a prototype of a Linux version created from zero, with Linux From Scratch⁹, was initiated. It was possible to verify that it would not be a truly safe solution in the short term, despite this technology makes it possible to create an operating system from scratch with the use of this organization scripts. Such outcome, to be considered secure, requires its certification and obtaining official recognition after a few years of testing and use by a significant sample of users. Regardless of the time, a version was effectively started and was submitted for testing and verification and will be considerate future work in post-research.

Considering the previous scenario, the scientifically correct would be to choose an open source base operating system, duly accredited and tested by the community and develop on it, as was performed with the mobile prototype. Initially the considerate option was to use an Ubuntu Server as this distribution is completely empty of any software and graphical environment, being possible to develop the prototype according to security needs. The previous approach has been shown to be complex and somewhat insecure, as ad-hoc choice of applications without a notion of the behaviour they possess and might have with other applications, could be a security issue in the future, as once again, the measurement of safety by use would require a few months with a large team for testing in order to find incompatibilities.

Considering the scenario previously described, the option was to use a stable version of Ubuntu 14.04 LTS for desktop, with large information about it in technology repositories. This version for desktops should have a long-term commitment of support from Canonical^(10) and extensive literature and usage in IEEE research papers, being able to securely remove all non-configurable and useless applications for the prototype usage.

Researching through the state of the art, each of the tools projected to be available in the prototype was individually studied for their safe use and upgradability in future versions. In general, it was intended to install various technologies and test them, to check if they cohabit in harmony, to know:

*   • Anonymous chat system like Pidgin and Torchat;
*   • Anonymous search engines such as DuckDuckGo;
*   • Bleachbleed data eliminator;
*   • ClamTK Av Solution;
*   • Cryptkeeper directory encryption;
*   • Cryptosetup LUKS Encryption Tool;
*   • Electron Bitcoin Wallet;
*   • HTTPS Everywhere Extension;
*   • Keys and Passwords base in Public Key Infrastructure;
*   • Tor Network circuits and browser;
*   • Ubuntu 14.04 LTS operating system, based on the Linux Debian system;
*   • Vidalia Tor browser.

Productive tools present in the prototype as:

*   • Audacity;
*   • ImageMagic.

To ensure that the methodology is robust and coherent, the process of removing all additional software that needs to communicate over the Web and incapable of adjustments to use the Tor Network to update or communicate was conducted. This process was executed also in the mobile prototype’s development.

The following items were removed from a wider list of deleted software:

*   • Account manager - User Account Manager;
*   • Appearance - Settings Manager (themes, icons, extra fonts, screen backgrounds);
*   • Audio player - RythmboxPlayer;
*   • Backup - Backup manager and data replication system for repository or other type;
*   • Device manager - Monitor Manager (manual colour and screen resolution Adjustment);
*   • Disk journal - Scanning system;
*   • Energy controller - Energy statistics system;
*   • File Manager - File Manager, namely the ability to manage and change any file that requires root authorization for modification;
*   • Games - Games that require internet;
*   • GUI - Unity Graphic Environment;
*   • Hardware manager - Additional hardware and driver Manager;
*   • Language Support - support in addition to Portuguese or English, be it graphic or literary resource;
*   • Mail - Thunderbird Mail Client;
*   • Network LDAP - Account Manager on the network;
*   • Office productivity - LibreOffice;
*   • Pictures gallery - Hotel Photo Manager;
*   • Print - Printer Manager and service that run natively associated with printing;
*   • Remote Desktop - Remina Remote Desktop Client;
*   • Screen - Screen Sharing system;
*   • Security tools - Spam Assassin anti-spam system;
*   • Video player - Video Player;
*   • Webcam - Webcam Support with animation software.

The list is long and extensive and is not limited to the above items because, in order to install the necessary components, it was first necessary to obtain an operating system that did not communicate with the outside unless the user instructed it to do so.

Using Wireshark from the laboratory set of tools, there wasn’t detected any attempts to communicate via http elsewhere without the user intention.

Once the previous objective was reached, it was necessary to install the Tor Network Proxy service and configure the proxy (SOCKS5) to run natively when starting the computer. This step differs from the mobile prototype due to the fact that Ubuntu possesses natively the ability to control socks communication. This way, whenever any application starts and needs to communicate recurring to internet, it will do so over the Tor Network, not exposing the user location and surrounding any censorship mechanism and above all, in an encrypted manner, TLSv1.2. For this, it was necessary to add the Tor software repository in an isolated resource:

*   deb http://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org utadsafe main
*   deb-src http://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org utadsafe main
*   gpg --keyserver keys.gnupg.net --recv 886DDD89
*   gpg --export A3C4F0F979CAA22CDBA8F512EE8CBC9E886DDD89 | sudo apt-key add -
*   tar xzf tor-0.2.6.10.tar.gz; cd tor-0.2.6.10
*   ./configure && make
*   $ apt-get update
*   $ apt-get install tor deb.torproject.org-keyring

After installation by a previously verified procedure, it was necessary to ensure that whenever using the apt-get-install method, a common command to install software from console to add software, it recurs only the network securely means, and for this purpose it was required to alter the sources.list file:

*   /etc/apt/sources.list
*   gedit /etc/apt/sources.list
*   deb http://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org utadsafe main
*   deb-src http://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org utadsafe main
*   gpg --keyserver keys.gnupg.net --recv 886DDD89 gpg --export A3C4F0F979CAA22CDBA8F512EE8CBC9E886DDD89 | sudo apt-key add -
*   sudo apt-get update
*   sudo apt-get install tor deb.torproject.org-keyring
*   sudo apt-get install apt-transport-tor
*   gedit /etc/apt/sources.list

This is an important step in the development of the prototype as, among others, the most important one is the installation and availability of the Tor Network as Web communication service.

After ensuring the above procedure, the production and common use applications and tools have been re-installed in an isolated manner within the operating system, thus guarantying individually that each one behaves appropriately.

One of the most important prototype’s configurations is the native iptables settings. In a working environment common to desktops, the possibility to adjust the iptables is common. In the mobile prototype and because mobile systems don’t have a firewall that enables changes, in the desktop prototype this was programmed manually.

In the desktop prototype, the need to fast change the iptables setting was circumvolved by installing a GUI for it, thus creating conditions to any eventual alteration. In the Firewall configuration were defined the following rules that allow blocking all traffic outside the ports defined in the firewall e.g., 443, 80, 8080 and all the other that it is possible to see in MIT Common port list^(11).

Despite the inclusion of a graphic environment for the firewall, the following command lines where imputed to control de iptables and then verifies over Firewall GUI:

*   • Block all traffic: 
    *   iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
    *   iptables -P INPUT DROP
    *   iptables -P FORWARD DROP
*   • Block network attacks: 
    *   iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp ! --tcp-flags SYN,RST,ACK SYN -m state --state NEW -j DROP
    *   iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m tcp ! --tcp-flags SYN,RST,ACK SYN -m state --state NEW -j DROP
*   • Drop traffic with invalid stat: 
    *   iptables -N drop\_invalid
    *   iptables -A OUTPUT -m state --state INVALID -j drop\_invalid
    *   iptables -A INPUT -m state --state INVALID -j drop\_invalid
    *   iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --sport 1:65535 --tcp-flags FIN,SYN,RST,PSH,ACK,URG NONE -j drop\_invalid
    *   iptables -A drop\_invalid -j LOG --log-level debug --log-prefix “INVALID state -- DENY “
    *   iptables -A drop\_invalid -j DROP
*   • Accept Tor output and Input: 
    *   iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 9001 -j ACCEPT
    *   iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 9050 -j ACCEPT
    *   iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 9001 -j ACCEPT
    *   iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 9050 -j ACCEPT

No shortcuts to the firewall are enabled in the prototype graphical environment, it is only accessible from the command line with the following command and disclaimed in the instruction’s readme file located in the desktop:

utadsafe@Ubuntu:~$ sudo gufw  
(sudo) password for utadsafe: 123

In conclusion, the following set of images shows the that the proposed methodology in the desktop prototype, likewise with the mobile prototype, had its scope achieved.

During the all process, communications have been monotonized via WireShark available in the lab with no results out of the pre-established that was to stop the leakage of users valuable and vital information to unknown subjects.

All communications go through the Tor Network in HTTPS forced traffic and if the user decides so, a second three-layer tunnels is established within the Tor Network. This provides two circles of identity in Tor, working in a double direction circle.

ANALYSIS OF END USER TESTS

This paragraph aims to present the results of the online survey conducted to evaluate the Methodology success through the testing of the Mobile and Desktop prototypes developed.

Two groups of subjects were selected based in two factors, their knowledge of technology and their active profession, and for this the author obtain the help of Altran Portugal World Class Centre and Industrialized Global Shore engineers, ISEP, IPCA and UTAD students and researchers. With this, this thesis acquires information from solid technology professionals, their empirical opinion and results after testing both prototypes. Finally, the common end user information based on their day-2-day operations with the prototypes through a specific scenario.

For the above analysis the two scenarios (desktop and mobile) were implemented in the project’s laboratory in Citrix in AWS Amazon, where the users could test and use the prototypes. Their responses are sonly based in that experience.

The privacy of the subjects was assure previously recurring to anonymity (if they choose this option) and in full respect of the GDPR. Important information like audience age and gender, area of training, knowledge of technology for setting up the host, host technical resources, bugs, professional opinion and other data was collected to learn from it.

The survey process was carried out and answered through the Web by 200 individuals out of 1000 solicitations, divided between above mentioned entities. Data collection was then processed in Microsoft Excel to build support charts recurring to PowerPivot technology and worked in IBM SPSS for accurate statistics.

In response to a survey placed online in the Google Forms Platform that can be found here: https://forms.gle/xMVf1SNWY6DrcjDU9, a total of 200 individuals agreed to test the prototypes and respond to the survey.

The characterizations of the subjects to test and survey was composed by three groups, group A, B and group C:

*   • A - Classroom presentations and form completions;
*   • B - Online demonstration and form completions;
*   • C - Classroom and Online presentation/demonstration and form completions.

In the Group A, six groups of twenty individuals attended to a technical demonstration in classroom. To the Group B, a resource was made available in the form of a video with the demonstration of use with settings, instructions and examples with practical use of the prototypes content and the remaining eighty individuals have participated. The Group C is a reference to subjects that participated in both types of demonstration and form completions. To all participants was given a guide script with tests to perform, available as annexes of this research.

In the classroom, both prototypes were set available via DVD or USB support and installed on the participants' computers for them to undergo quality, usability and security effectiveness testing for location masking, aspects protection techniques in the available browsers and other security aspects concerning the use of prototype applications.

For the remaining subjects, a lab was made available in a virtualized environment on AWS Amazon's infrastructure for them to undergo quality, usability and security effectiveness testing for location masking, aspects protection techniques in the available browsers and other security aspects concerning the use of prototype applications. To all participants was set available both options for them to provide feedback.

Aside of the many technical testing questions several regarding the methodology were placed and the results are as follow.

To the question “Methodology cost vs tools and software cost”, 97% of participants agree that the proposed methodology is more cost effectively than the use of the technologies displayed in the previous point in their work environment. The remaining 3% do not agree to this statement.

To the question “Comfort and willingness to use the methodology”, 89,5% indicated that they would feel comfortable and the remaining 10,5% stated the opposite.

To the question “Advising the use of the methodology”, 97,5% of participants indicate that would recommend the use of a prototype like operating system, and the remaining 2,5% the opposite. Being the prototypes the materialization of the proposed methodology, this leads to conclude that the expert participants would recommend such specific methodology.

To the question “Willingness to configure systems with the methodology”, 94% of the participants indicated willingness to configure a system with similar characteristics as the prototypes, 6% stated otherwise.

To the question “Use of a methodology as guideline”, 98% of the participants stated that very clear as the remaining 2% defended the negative possibility.

To the question “Confidence in methodology origin”, 98% of participants inform that they feel comfort knowing that the proposed methodology possesses and academic and scientific origin, has the remaining 3% indicate otherwise.

To the question “Methodology recommendation”, 99,5% of IT professionals, aware that the prototypes reflect a methodology, state that they would recommend the methodology to their colleagues. The remaining 0,5%, which consist a residual margin indicate that would not recommend the methodology to their colleagues.

CONCLUSIONS AND FUTURE RESEARCH

This book chapter aimed to demonstrate the result of a solid, scientific, serious and above all useful study. Technology is advancing at a fast pace and computer security for most users, despite being the order of the day, is left with the headlines of more or less sweeping news, rather than the concept of global participation or inclusion of users in the decision chain, as they are considered as reactive service customers, such as antivirus program customers and therefore a source of revenue, and are within a circle that profits from this concept, the reactive one.

Computer security is a reactive concept because of its complexity. It is by reacting to an event that is always behind the problem rather than anticipating it. Admittedly, organizations have taken very important steps towards creating standards that allows the control of information systems and allows them to have elements that are not common to find and apply in a traditionally domestic market.

It is up to the users to understand through their computer skills or knowledge what mechanisms exist to protect them, and which threats exist beyond the most common as computer viruses. It is commonly understood that most users do not understand what a man-in-the-middle attack is or what a data offset of a fibber optic ring consists of. It is common for most users not to know what a VPN is or what a proxy is that checks a certain type of addresses to see which ones are secure or not. This puts ordinary users in a position of vulnerability that this work intends and can successful mitigate.

The methodology embodied in two prototypes, an operating system desktop and mobile operating system, were able to overcome the problem of online insecurity created by the capture of private information or access locks by censorship mechanisms.

In the development of the methodology and consequently in the prototypes, there was always the concern to create a unique solution among those that can be observed in the state of the art, but with a solid academic background and above all capable of having additional research viability so that the project won’t stop as did the existing alternatives that are quite outdated, despite their academic origin.

This is an investigation that began in 2013 and came to an end in 2019 with much effort and investment from several nationally renowned universities, namely Universidade de Trás os Montes e Alto Douro, Instituto Superior de Engenharia do Porto and Instituto Politécnico do Cávado e do Ave. All participated in the creation of laboratory resources and academic resources to achieve a concrete goal, the POSMASWEB - Paranoid Operating Systems Methodology for Anonymous & Secure Web Browsing.

Analysing the results of the questionnaires, the adherence to the concept and the final product is always around 90% of acceptance, which in itself indicates, and considering the high technical level of the participants, that this research promotes preventive and non-recurring computer security, and that some of the successes are only achievable in the normal context, using expensive and complex security systems and mechanisms that this methodology alleviates, according to feedback from participants.

As future work, the prospect is to create a laboratory to continue and deepen the research that resulted from this thesis. A wider range of individuals and more complex questions need to be performed in order to create the ground for future work. Three institutions were approached to enable the creation of a project in the form of a permanent laboratory, which through the use of economic fund applications would allow the creation of a permanent research team, each element with their individual master’s or doctoral line of investigation within this thesis scope.

Several methodology-based prototypes have been developed that require time and maturation to assert themselves as more solid alternatives, namely those consisting of operating systems created from zero base, but due to time constraints it was not possible to make all tests viable due to lack of technical resources.

The authors of this research have initiated talks with leading operating system development organizations today, namely Canonical and Microsoft, to include the application of the methodology as an additional security mode in their operating systems. This proposal lacks a solid structure and specific laboratory resources to further consider the suggestion, which is clearly in the authors interests.

KEY TERMS AND DEFINITIONS

Backdoor: Backdoor in the literary translation. It means a hidden door for access to a program or equipment.

Commercial Off-the-Shelf: Software ready to use, purchasable by standard in commercial spaces.

Cracker: Name of people who create and modify computer software and hardware in order to destroy information and use it for their own advantage, seeking recognition, insider information or even monetary compensations.

Eavesdropping: It literally means listening in a hidden way.

Exploit: Leveraging a software or equipment vulnerability.

Firewall: It is a device from a network of computers that has the function of regulating network traffic between unrelated networks and preventing the transmission and/or reception of harmful or unauthorized data from one network to another.

Hacker: It is a term attributed to people who create and modify computer software and hardware in order to acquire information. Depending on the type of hacker, it can use the information he collects, holding it to inform organizations of inherent vulnerabilities or use it for your own benefit, seeking recognition, insider information, or even monetary compensations.

Live DVD: Is a complete bootable computer installation including operating system which runs directly from a DVD-ROM.

Malware: Malware is a program designed to cause damage or to illegally access information on computer systems.

Password: Secret piece of data that is used in conjunction with a username to access private content or privileged systems.

Spyware: Programs that are typically related to advertising and exchanging information from the client computer to a server, without the knowledge of it. They are a kind of non-destructive virus and are sometimes not detectable by antivirus applications, but rather by new applications called “Anti-spyware”.

Trojan: Trojan or Trojans, a malware that acts just like in the history of Trojan Horse, entering the computer and creating a port for a possible invasion.

Virtual Server: A virtual server allows to get all the functionality of a physical server without resorting to an independent physical machine. The virtual server takes advantage of the host machine hardware (service server), using it as its own. Despite the loss of substantial performance, this technique allows to have multiple independent servers within one machine.

Virus: Program that runs on a machine with or without user knowledge and that targets the integrity, availability or confidentiality of the information.

# Chapter 24
