# Chapter 27

Threat Analysis and Countermeasures

*   Ramanpreet Kaur  
    Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana, Slovenia
*   Tomaž Klobučar  
    Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana, Slovenia
*   Dušan Gabrijelčič  
    Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana, Slovenia

ABSTRACT

This chapter is concerned with the identification of the privacy threats to provide a feedback to the users so that they can make an informed decision based on their desired level of privacy. To achieve this goal, Solove’s taxonomy of privacy violations is refined to incorporate the modern challenges to the privacy posed by the evolution of social networks. This work emphasizes on the fact that the privacy protection should be a joint effort of social network owners and users, and provides a classification of mitigation strategies according to the party responsible for taking these countermeasures. In addition, it highlights the key research issues to guide the research in the field of privacy preservation. This chapter can serve as a first step to comprehend the privacy requirements of online users and educate the users about their choices and actions in social media.

INTRODUCTION

The ubiquitous presence of social networks in the people’s lives has led to unprecedented privacy issues as evident by the reported privacy scandals (Sanders & Patterson, 2019). The users are unwittingly relying on the social networking site for their personal information, relationships, participation in society, and even for broadcasting pithy news messages to others. This will enable the attackers to steal sensitive information, spread and amplify disinformation, inciting violence, and lowering levels of trust in media and democratic institution. Thus, the researchers and privacy practitioners should move beyond adoption and focus on the privacy implications of the user engagement with the social networking sites as the owners of these networks only strive for an active user base and consider the user engagement as the only metric of success.

The privacy risks posed by social networking sites range from the interfering and exploiting social interactions to the more sophisticated data collection, processing, distribution and privacy invasion by the owners of networking sites, third-party applications and the attackers as shown in Figure 1. Solove (Solove, 2006) has argued that privacy violations involve a variety of harmful and problematic activities. This chapter refines the Solove’s taxonomy (Solove, 2006) of information privacy violation to incorporate the challenges posed by social networking sites and provides taxonomy of countermeasures for privacy protection. Together, they serve as a useful checklist for a user to determine the priorities for the selection of privacy control. This taxonomy can also be used by the researchers to answer two important questions:

*   • What are the existing privacy threats in the online social networks? And why is it a difficult problem to handle?
*   • What are the unsolved problems and how one can contribute to the privacy field?

| Figure 1. Activities that invade privacy |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch027.f01](i/ch027.f01.png) |
| --- |

This chapter mainly focuses on studying the privacy threats on Facebook, though it can easily be generalized to the other social networks. It is organized as follows: Section II describes the importance of privacy in the social networks along with the potential attacks. Section III adapts the Solove’s taxonomy (Solove, 2006) of the privacy violation in the social network’s context along with a detailed description of each threat. Next, Section IV provides a taxonomy of the different approaches to mitigate the privacy risks on the social networks. Section V summarizes the findings and provides the relationship between the threat actors and the privacy threats discussed in the previous sections. Section VI outlines the future research directions for the service providers in the field of social networks and Section VII concludes this study.

BACKGROUND

Before discussing the privacy threats in the social networks, we will describe the importance of privacy in social networks along with the technological aspects of privacy and data protection. These two aspects serve as a basic concept to understand the implications of social network use and motivate the users to protect their privacy in the social networking sites.

Privacy

Privacy is a multidimensional concept made of different ideas regarding the personal information, freedom from intrusion and protection from the searches and surveillance. In 1967, Westin (Westin, 1968) has defined the privacy in terms of the control against the disclosure of the information claim of individuals, groups, or institutions to determine for themselves when, how, and to what extent information about them is communicated to others. However, Müller has defined privacy as the possibility to control the distribution and use of personal data (Müller, 2006). This definition has focused on the management of the information. Following the definitions of Westin and Muller, in this research work, we have seen privacy as the generalized notion of management of private information. In other words, in order to protect the privacy of the individual, autonomy and control should be provided over private information with the possibility to grant or deny access, collection, processing and dissemination. Although researchers and other professionals are working to ensure the privacy of individuals, violations are still an important issue in people’s activities and businesses.

Privacy in Social Networks

The evolution of social networks has led to many modern challenges to the privacy of its users, e.g. tracking, profiling and identity theft. These challenges are more complex than the simple concept of intrusion and exposure. A simple example is, privacy laws can defend exposure by restraining the sites from the publication of sensitive information about its users, but the social networks are using this information for targeted advertising without actually publishing it. They have entirely different characteristics as compared to the traditional privacy problems.

Most of the social networking sites have perceived privacy as a freedom of unwanted access or desired inaccessibility as evident from their privacy policy and term of use (Van Schaik et al., 2018). They will treat the sharing of private information as a voluntary loss of privacy. However, this concept fails to distinguish between the disclosure of information to a group of people and disclosure to the whole world. This concept of privacy has raised serious concerns regarding the important role of user involvement in privacy settings, the role of third parties and the user data commercialization by the platform owners. Moreover, this concept of privacy has not considered modern challenges posed by the technology such as web tracking (Cozza et al., 2020), location tracking (Li et al., 2014), automated profiling (Mavriki & Karyda, 2019; Poo et al., 2003) and identity theft (Gross & Acquisti, 2005).

Protecting the privacy of an individual in a social network seems to be an oxymoron as the main purpose of participating in the social networks is to share personal information in order to maintain relationships and expand social circle. This personal information sharing attracts hackers, data miners, third party applications, political parties, businesses and even the government agencies to misuse this private information for their personal gain. Even friends or other users on the social networking sites can endanger the privacy of an individual by cyberstalking, reputation damage, or harassment (Kayes & Iamnitchi, 2017).

The privacy threats on the social networks are reported in different surveys (Kayes & Iamnitchi, 2017; Fire et al., 2014a; Pham et al., 2017; Shaoo & Gupta, 2019). But all these surveys have mainly studied these threats in the form of attacks on the security, reputation and profiling. However, none of the existing work has concentrated on the identification of activities that pose these privacy problems. Our research focuses on the identification of privacy threats based on the different kinds of activities that impinge on the privacy and aids the better understanding of privacy to the users so that they can make an informed decision based on the desired level of privacy.

Personal Data

In order to protect the privacy of an individual, data protection is designed to regulate the conditions under which data can be collected, processed and disseminated. According to the European Union general data protection regulation (Hoofnagle et al., 2019), personal data refers to any information relating to an identified or at least identifiable person, where an identifiable person is the one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identification number or to one or more factors specific to his physical, physiological, mental, economic, cultural or social identity. Some examples of the personal data are: name, address, email address, IP address, user profile, browsing behavior and location data. The directive has also listed a special category of personal data that pose a greater risk when processed and named it as the sensitive data (Hoofnagle et al., 2019) such as the personal data that expose ethnic or racial origin, religious belief, political orientation, mental health details, physical health and sexual life.

Nowadays, as the online interactions creates a large amount of data in the form of traces and every piece of data is related to a person somehow, so the differentiation between the personal and non-personal data is difficult. So, in this chapter, the term personal data refers to all types of data that relates to an individual in the direct or indirect manner.

Threat Actors

A threat actor is defined as an entity that intentionally or unintentionally attempts to or conducts a malicious activity to compromise the privacy of the users. As the nature and impact of the privacy threats also depend on the threat actor, thus, identification of the threat actors further aids the effective implementation of the privacy control. This section examines five important categories of threat actors: users, connections, social network platform, third-party applications, and invader as shown in Figure 2.

| Figure 2. Threat actors |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch027.f02](i/ch027.f02.png) |
| --- |

*   1\. Users: The users are the ones utilizing the services provided by the social networking site. The careless and irresponsible data sharing and third-party application use along with the lack of technical literacy and insufficient privacy settings causes privacy issues and leads to threats in the social networks (Millham & Atkin, 2018).
*   2\. Connections: The connections are the acquittances of the user on the social networking site. The social circle of a person in the online world is very diverse as compared to the physical world. Moreover, the term connections are ambiguous in the online world and used to represent all the social connections without differentiating between family, friends, soulmate, acquaintances and strangers. The privacy risk posed by the connections varies from unintentional exposure by tagging to the trolling and intentional exposure of sensitive information (Zubiaga et al., 2018).
*   3\. Invader: The invaders are the malicious or non-malicious users, who can pose a threat to the private information of social networking users for the personal satisfaction, law enforcement, spying, reputation harm, or for financial gain. These threats range from the well-known identity theft (Navarro & Jasinski, 2014) to the more serious state sponsored threats to endanger the democratic rights of an individual (Mayer, 2018).
*   4\. Social Networking Site or Platform: The social networking site provides a means of communication to its users to participate in society. They are actively being used to seek and share information with a large audience. The business orientation and inherent design flaws significantly affect the privacy of its users. The threats posed by social networking site range from data scraping to more sophisticated appropriation attack (Fire et al., 2014a).
*   5\. Third Party Applications: The third-party applications are the programs that can interact with the social network such as quizzes, online polls, games. The social networking sites allow the seamless integration of user’s profile data with the third-party applications. These third-party applications receive the owner’s privileges once the user installs the application, regardless of the actual application needs. These applications pose a serious privacy risk to users as the applications are not covered by the privacy policy and a user has no control over how they will use his/her private data. The threats posed by these applications vary from simple data harvesting to the more serious threat to the democracy by spreading misinformation and opinion manipulation (Adrienne & David, 2008).

TAXONOMY OF PRIVACY THREATS

Identification of privacy threats in the online social networks is an important task as billions of users are contributing a large amount of information and are unfamiliar with the underlying privacy risk. Therefore, significant efforts are needed for the identification of the privacy threats and providing recommendations for the social network users to protect their security and privacy. This section will classify the privacy threats into four categories based on the different types of activities that impinge on privacy. These activities are: data collection, data processing, information dissemination, and privacy invasion as shown in Figure 3. The categories are further refined according to the underlying mechanism and intentions behind the conduct of these activities. Our threat taxonomy is refinement of the Solove’s (Solove, 2006) taxonomy of information privacy threats by introducing new digital privacy violations, posed by the evolution of online social networks. For example, web tracking technologies are able to track and relate the activities, interactions and content of people. Another relevant example is automated profiling, which creates profiles and enables prediction (or discrimination) of people's behavior, attitudes and interests. It is important to note that these issues have different characteristics compared to traditional privacy issues; they are the product of digital information flows, architectural design choices of systems and online social interactions. These types of violations, which are not known to Solove (Solove, 2006), will be further analyzed later in this chapter. Privacy violations lead to the conception and application of privacy, which, when properly applied, brings benefits to information management. The detailed description of each category along with the associated threats is described below.

| Figure 3. Taxonomy of privacy threats |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch027.f03](i/ch027.f03.png) |
| --- |

Data Collection

There are various methods to collect the data on the online social networks: mandatory disclosure, voluntary disclosure, unannounced acquisition, and information deduction by the attack. However, the intent of the person collecting the information is not necessarily harmful. The different ways to collect the information are as follows.

Information Access

The accessibility in the social networks refers to the easy access to the user’s basic profile information so that the old friends or new colleagues can easily search for the person to get connected or share information using the underlying social network platform. It is generally harmless and one of the necessary features of a social networking site to grow the individual’s social circle.

Monitoring

The monitoring consists of a set of actions used to track the personal information, behavior and communication patterns to provide better services or to protect it from cyber threats. For example: Facebook uses the data about the devices the user has used to log in, to block the sign in attempt from an attacker (Vaithyasubramanian et al., 2015).

Surveillance

The social network site, third party service providers, government agency, a friend or a malicious user can watch or record someone’s activities without their consent. This is known as surveillance. The surveillance can expose the individual to various threats like cyber stalking, personality profiling, investigation without search warrant, etc. An example of surveillance in social networking sites is online social tracking via “like”, “+1”, “tweet” or other buttons. These buttons work with cookies, which enable tracking of the user across different sites and recording their interests and behavior (Cofone, 2017). The increased usage of social networking applications and mobile social networks can further aid the user tracking by providing the real time information with the help of device-generated data such as location, device id, contacts etc.

Mandatory Disclosure

With social networking sites, in order to join, the user has to provide some mandatory information like email, name, date of birth etc. This information is then used to construct their profile and send notification and can even be sold for the business gain.

Social Engineering

A malicious user can trick the social network users to make security mistakes and share their personal information. The most widely used attacks for this purpose are phishing and clickjacking attacks (Caldwell, 2013).

Data Scraping

The data scraping is the process of exporting a large amount of data available from the public profile, saving it and making it available to use for different purposes. The scraped data can be used for research, marketing, spread disinformation, opinion manipulation or to perform social engineering attacks. The data scraping will increase the accessibility of the information. This will not create a new harm, but increase the likelihood. In 2020, an illegal scraping operation on Facebook exposed the data of almost 267 million users (Bischoff, 2020). This data has exposed the name, phone number and user ids of Facebook users and leave them vulnerable to spam and phishing attacks.

Data Processing

The data processing is a privacy threat as it can be exploited as a tool to use and manipulate the collected data for any other purpose rather than its intended use. The data processing activities can be classified into three types: Data Harvesting, Information Aggregation, and Insecurity. These activities are described in detail below.

Data Harvesting

The data harvesting involves the collection, processing and storage of data for future rewards. The sensitivity of the personal information and behavior available on the social media makes automated data harvesting a pressing issue. The data available on the social media has commercial, research and political value as evident from the recent incidents (Allcott & Gentzkow, 2017). The data harvesting can be further categorized into five types based on its purpose:

*   1\. Business: The business of the social media sites is based on the surveillance of its users. The data collected by the surveillance will be processed and then used for their commercial interests by behavioral advertising, location advertising or sharing user data with different business providers (Bonchi et al., 2011; Kosinski et al., 2014).
*   2\. Research: The public data available on the social networks such as public profiles, public tweets, photos or messages, public groups or community page information can be extracted using the company’s API (Giglietto et al., 2012). But the social scientists have to follow the social networking site’s policy for the usage of their data.
*   3\. Service Betterment: The social network sites can use the data and behavior information of their user to implement new features in order to improve their services and user experience with their applications. For example, Facebook is continuously adding new features such as friend suggestions, facial recognition and all these services access your personal data for implementation.
*   4\. Malicious Use: The sophisticated hackers are using the social network data to house the social data and sell it to others for financial benefit (Moore, 2019). This data can be used for social engineering attacks or to regulate the future developments and the behavior of the society by generating fake news and advertisement.
*   5\. Political Use: The social network data are increasingly being used by the political parties for user profiling to target them with more personalized political advertisements. Many incidents have reported the use of online social networks as a psychological warfare tool by the political parties (Barfar, 2019).

Information Aggregation

The aggregation involves the consolidation of user content when he/she socializes on the social media or consolidation of user information from different social network sites to compromise his/her privacy. The in-network and cross-network information aggregation is explained as follows:

*   1\. In-network Information Aggregation: From the profile creation to the socializing on the social networks, the users of the networks share a part of their personal information, their present viewpoint, or their behavior patterns over time. A careful investigator can easily aggregate all this information and extract useful information about their social and personal life, which is otherwise not evident from its profile. This information about their behavior, physical and mental health, political and religious views, their current friends can then be used for financial or political benefits, reputation harm or for harassment (Li et al., 2017).
*   2\. Cross-network Information Aggregation: Li et al. have shown that the users tend to use multiple social networking sites for different purposes ranging from a professional network to a dating site (Li et al., 2017). However, they do not want to mix up the information from different contexts. But, due to the open nature of social networking site and availability of more sophisticated information retrieval and aggregation techniques, their privacy is at stake.

Insecurity

The insecurity refers to the improper protection and handling of personal information by the social networking sites. Most of the data breaches reported on the social networking sites are due to their design flaws, improper access control and security measures. Recently, millions of user’s personal details have been exposed as a result of compromised Facebook’s developer API (Bischoff, 2020).

Information Dissemination

The third area of privacy threats is a personal information leak or threat of such leak. This information leak can be classified into two types based on the intention behind the information dissemination: Accidental or Deliberate. In the Accidental information dissemination, the victim’s information is not disclosed intentionally. Whereas, in case of deliberate information dissemination, the victim’s privacy is disclosed purposefully for personal or financial benefits. This deliberate dissemination is further categorized according to the underlying mechanism used to disclose the information: Data disclosure, Data publication, Information diffusion, and Distortion.

Accidental Information Dissemination

The accidental information dissemination is unintentional disclosure of the personal information from the user or his/her social connections. There are various ways in which the personal information can be disclosed as described below:

*   1\. Tagging: The vulnerable friends or friends with weak privacy settings can expose the social network user to the privacy threats by tagging him/her while posting an update or picture (Rathore et al., 2017). Thus, even a social network user with most stringent privacy settings is vulnerable to the privacy attack. The continuous expansion of social networks and diversity of individual’s social circle further complicates the process of securing the privacy.
*   2\. Updates using phone disseminate lot of meta data information along with location: The luxury of posting their updates on the go leverage the social networking consumers to use the mobile applications of social networking sites. However, the always-on location services on the mobile phones and meta data in social networking posts have turned our mobile phone into a personal tracking device (Sadeh et al., 2009). So, the real time information sharing through mobile social networks can result in privacy breaches and new opportunities for the invaders.

Deliberate Information Dissemination

The deliberate information dissemination is the process of sharing or leaking the private information for personal or financial benefit. The potential sources of privacy threats in this area include the following:

*   1\. Data Disclosure: The social networking sites will generate their revenue either by sharing the personal details of their users or by hyper targeted advertisement by recording every second of the lives of their unwitting users. Facebook applications are actively leaking personal identifying information about its users to the advertising and internet tracking companies (Augusto & Simões, 2017). They are justifying this leakage by making the user accept certain terms and conditions during the installation process and once he/she clicks allow, they will share these access tokens with advertisers to give them access to personal profile data including chat details and the photos. However, these terms and conditions do not announce the transfer of the user data to the third-party applications and pose significant risk to the privacy and safety of online users. The issue of online privacy gets more complex as the social widgets “Like”, “tweet”, “+1” and other buttons are increasingly being used by other e-commerce sites and facilitate the tracking of users across different sites (Cofone, 2017). This will allow the complete access to your interests and online shopping behavior and rudely invade the internet privacy.
*   2\. Data Publication: The data collected and collated by social networking sites could be used by researchers, sociologists or epidemiologists for science and security, health, business, crisis management and for other datamining tasks. This data contains a lot of private information of its participants. Thus, the publication of this data is a critical issue. Researchers are currently working on the anonymization and sanitization techniques for the publication of data so that the privacy of user’s preserved and the needs of data miners are satisfied (Yang & Cudré-Mauroux, 2018).
*   3\. Information Diffusion: Online social networks have provided a platform for everyone to share their viewpoints and information with a large audience in the fraction of seconds without spending any money. The dark side of this information spreading is the diffusion of private facts, rumors and fake information in the society (Zubiaga et al., 2018). Although, the perceptive user does not disclose his/her personal information on the social networks, but he/she is not aware about the consequences of their simple like or comment on the news or any specific post. This lack of awareness is easily targeted by the malicious users to spread fake information and rumors on the social networking sites and to disclose the political orientation, interests and behavior of the user. The most recent example is malicious coronavirus disinformation campaigns by hostile states and cybercriminals for financial damage and to promote dangerous guidance (Guirakhoo, 2020).
*   4\. Distortion: The online social networks are being criticized for the diffusion of fake information and rumors. But a little is known about the intentional distortion of the content to damage reputation, perform scams, and avoid censorship. Recently, Elyashar et al. (2020) have reported a vulnerability of Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn networks that can be easily exploited to manipulate the content display. This vulnerability allows the updating of link previews without any notifications or loss of social capital.

Invasion

The invasion of privacy encompasses the unwelcome intrusion into the user’s domain. There are various ways in which the social networks directly invade the privacy of its users:

Identity Theft

The potential of social networks is often misused by the attackers, who extract sensitive private information of an unwitting user and use it to impersonate real user. This is known as identity theft in the broader term. Moreover, the social networking websites lack the basic mechanism to verify the identity of the user during account formation. Thus, a malicious user can easily clone the identity of the victim and use his credentials for deception, disinformation, advertisement, distortion or information collection. The well-known attacks in this category are profile cloning (Fire et al., 2014^b), Evil Twin attack (Navarro & Jasinski, 2014), spear phishing (Caldwell, 2013), whaling (Hu et al., 2015), sybil attack (Yang et al., 2014) and dumpster diving attack (Heartfield & Loukas, 2015).

Exposure

In the online social networks, the privacy of the users is impacted by the exposure of their information to other users. In this section, we are not concerned with the exposure of information due to design or user behavior rather we emphasize on the intentional exposure of the sensitive information about the user by a friend or acquaintances. The friends can tag the user in inappropriate post or post any inappropriate remarks on your profile and anybody can send you some inappropriate content in your message box. Thus, user’s friends and acquaintances have the ability to expose his/her physical and emotional attributes on a public platform.

Cyber-Vetting

The social-media surveillance has been actively used by the governments and potential employers to investigate about the user (Hanasono, 2013). According to the privacy advocates, this is a gross intrusion into an individual’s privacy and an infringement on people’s freedom to express themselves.

Cyberespionage

The wealth of public information available on the social media has been utilized by the state sponsored cyber groups to device automated spear phishing campaigns for target governments and military personnel. The social media is a popular weapon for politically motivated cyber-attacks as evident from the incidents related to the Russian efforts to manipulate Facebook and Twitter during and after the 2016 presidential elections (Mayer, 2018). The impact of these attacks varies from defamation of an individual to the theft of military plans and technological innovations. Thus, governments need to take stringent measures to regulate the privacy requirements of social networks due to political and military risks associated with social media weaponizing.

Tracking

Tracking user activities is a major threat to the privacy of the users. But, the viability of the online social network’s business model is on collecting personal data and using it for targeted or behavioral advertising (Binns & Bietti, 2019; Galán et al., 2019). Moreover, the increased usage of mobile social networking applications, lack of understanding of privacy policies, inherent data sharing capability between different applications and misconfiguration of privacy settings of the user account and mobile devices makes mobile social networking a surveillance application that can track the user navigation and their web surfing behavior. This risk becomes more severe as the boundary between online social networks and location-based services is blurred.

The social networking sites, third party applications, government agencies and malicious users can track the individuals’ activities, interactions, behavior and mobility over time. The traditional way of tracking the individual’s activities on the internet is web tracking (Li et al., 2014). Web tracking is the practice used by the website owners to follow the individual’s activities and interactions across multiple sites by using cookies and sharing it with others for the financial and business gain. The social networking sites further endanger the user privacy by giving away his or her name, friends and profile information to these tracking websites by including an advertising and tracking code in a browser. The proliferation of smartphones, further complicates the problem by giving access to the device related data along with a large amount of real time information about the behavior and communication patterns including the location history of an individual. This form of tracking can result in surveillance and can also endanger the physical privacy of the individual. The ease of traceability in social networks encourages cyber stalkers and online predators, and increases the risk of physical attacks.

Profiling

Another privacy challenge in the social networks is the automated profiling, which will intelligently process the personal data of users to assess their behavior, interests, health, economic situation and attitude. The automated profiling is based on the collection and processing of the personal and behavior data to find the co-relation between different databases in order to predict the personality of the person as shown in Figure 4. The automated profiling is increasingly being used by the researchers, businesses, political parties, malicious attackers, and even state sponsored cyber groups.

The profiling can be of two types: static and dynamic profiling (Poo et al., 2003). The static profiling is based on the analysis of user’s static profile. The quality of static profiling insights will degrade over time. Dynamic profiling is the process of observing the activities and actions of the user over time to predict their interests. Moreover, the mobile applications supplement the user’s information disclosure in one application with other applications, location data and even their social contacts by making them accept application permission requests. These mobile applications constantly watch the user’s activities and share this data with third-party applications for tracking and advertising. The profiling of individuals or group of individuals is usually performed using data aggregation techniques as explained in detail in section 3.2.2. The basic and well-known attacks in this category are inference attack (Cai et al., 2016), de-anonymization attack (Qian et al., 2017), cyber-vetting (Melton et al., 2017), targeted advertising (Binns & Bietti, 2019; Galán et al., 2019), political propaganda (Grimme et al., 2017), speculation attack (Zhang et al., 2010), illation attack (Mislove et al., 2010), espionage (Zhang et al., 2010) and social-engineering attacks (Krombholz et al., 2015).

RECOMMENDATIONS

Privacy protection has become one of the most critical issues in the age of social media. The findings of this research show that it is very difficult to achieve the acceptable level of privacy and much of the effort will be required from the user. However, this does not deny the fact that the privacy protection should be the joint effort of social network owners and the users (Fischer-Hübner & Berthold, 2017; Seničar et al., 2003). In this section, we will discuss the different approaches to mitigate the privacy risks on the social networks. As most of the identified privacy risks are posed by the carelessness of the users and inherent design flaws and business orientation of the platform owners, so we are emphasizing on the information and education of the users about the value of their privacy and the possibilities of the self-protection along with the steps and countermeasures for a social network platform by laying out easy to follow recommendations to ensure their privacy. Based on this, recommendations are classified into two main categories: Suggestions for the users and suggestions for the platforms owners as shown in Figure 5. The suggestions for the users will specify the easy to apply methods and instructions that the users of the social networks can adopt to make them resilient to the security and privacy violations. The suggestions for the platforms include the countermeasures that the social networking platforms can implement to provide a safer and trustworthy platform to its users.

| Figure 5. Different approaches to mitigate privacy risk |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch027.f05](i/ch027.f05.png) |
| --- |

Suggestions for the Users of the Social Networks

Most of the social network users lack a basic understanding of the social network technologies, mobile devices and applications, data they collect, and consequences of sharing their private and false information (Millham & Atkin, 2018). This will leave them vulnerable to the privacy and security violations. The very first step for the privacy protection is to enlighten the users about the social networks and their unlimited consequences, as they are responsible for protecting their information. This section will educate the users about the importance of privacy and responsible behavior on the social networking sites. Here, we will frame the behavior, technical and operational suggestions for the users to mitigate or prevent the privacy violations while using the social networks. As every user has the personalized privacy requirements which can vary over time, thus a user can handle a varying degree of privacy requirements by controlling their behavior, operation and technical preferences as shown in Figure 6. From the Figure 6, it is clear that the privacy of users depends on three dimensions: privacy awareness, degree of sociability and the privacy control. If the user is not aware about the privacy risks and is very social with no privacy settings the user’s privacy is at stake.

| Figure 6. User Privacy Control |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-5728-0.ch027.f06](i/ch027.f06.png) |
| --- |

Behavioral Suggestions

To ensure the privacy and safety, the online users have to behave responsibly while using the online social networks. Each user has an absolute control over the information they want to publish and who to be friends with. But once the information got published, it is considered as public and can be distributed, copied or repurposed without the owner’s knowledge (Debatin, 2011). So, a responsible user should have an informed concern about their privacy and should avoid ignorant behavior on social networks. The following guidelines need to be followed by the privacy literate user:

*   1\. Only mandatory information disclosure: The first step towards the privacy protection is sharing only the required information and avoid using full name and email that is being used for individual’s financial records and work. The information such as date of birth, physical address and phone numbers make the user vulnerable to various attacks such as social engineering attacks, identity theft, phishing attacks and many more (Salahdine & Kaabouch, 2019). The basic requirement to ensure the privacy is to expose only limited personal information and avoid giving access to address book, camera and microphone. If a user is considering a new feature, then he/she should carefully read the terms and conditions to understand what can be done with this information. Some users will advocate the use of privacy settings over the concept of limited sharing. But the technical privacy settings will only provide the spatial access barriers that can be bypassed by malicious attackers. Thus, it is always advisable to share only limited details on the social platform to maintain the integrity of the information.
*   2\. Caution while accepting new connection: One stranger in the user’s social media circle may endanger his/her personal details, pictures, post and compromise the privacy of his/her social media friends and family. Moreover, the possibility to misrepresent the identity (cloned account) and motivation, may further complicate the problem. So, users should always carefully investigate the person who has sent the request and report the suspicious accounts to the social network site. In order to protect the privacy and safety of children and teens, motivate them to limit the people who are allowed to contact them and educate them to be cautious about the information they reveal to the strangers through chat or agreeing to meet them in person.
*   3\. Stay vigilant and educated: The users of the social media sites should stay vigilant about the possible dangers on the social media and ways to strengthen their privacy by technical, operational and cautious behavioral means. With the increased sophistication of hackers and new ways to exploit the privacy, staying vigilant is the key to protect the privacy in the digital world.
*   4\. Stay updated about the terms of service: The social networking sites are accused of changing their privacy policies and terms of service regularly to wear down the user vigilance in maintaining the desired level of privacy settings (Turban et al., 2018). Moreover, the updated features and default opt-in option for them in the privacy policy further complicate the privacy protection of careless users. So, every user should regularly review their privacy settings and terms of service to control their privacy.

Operational Suggestions

The setting up and operating an account on the social networking site can put user’s privacy at risk as he/she is sharing his/her personal information online. Thus, a user should exercise caution while browsing social sites as it is often difficult to check the legitimacy of the accounts, information and third-party applications. This section will guide the users to choose security over convenience and recommend the practices to be followed to boost their digital privacy and security:

*   1\. Avoid social login: Most of the social networking sites encourages the third-party websites to allow the people to use their social account for login or creating accounts (Krämer et al., 2019). This functionality not only creates a single point of failure that can compromise user’s security across several sites, but it will also authorize these sites to share their information and activities for targeted advertising. Thus, the users of social networks are advised not to use social login as the security and privacy of this feature is doubtful.
*   2\. Always log out: The social networks are designed to keep the user logged in. Thus, most of the social networking sites either have longer session time out or do not have it at all. Keeping a browser session open provides a perfect avenue for hackers to access the user’s social account. The possible consequences vary from simple snooping to session hijacking to take control of their account (Bernard et al., 2012). Thus, social media users are advised to always log off your system when you are done with it.
*   3\. Be selective with the audience: The biggest pitfall of social media is the danger of spreading user’s personal information to the public. Almost all the social networking sites allow the user to control who can see their post. Thus, a perceptive user should always be selective with the intended audience of their shared post and should consider the possible consequences of sharing their information on the social platform.
*   4\. Close unused social media account: The more unused accounts users are hanging around; the more targets hackers will get to aim at. These unused accounts will not only expose their personal details, but also provide a route to more sensitive and more important accounts if users are sharing usernames and passwords or using single sign on feature (Krämer et al., 2019). So, the users are advised to delete all the unused social media accounts and be careful about the option to deactivate and delete account options. As the deactivation will keep their data available on the social media server.
*   5\. Principle of self-restrain: Every social network user except the business users should follow the principle of self-restrain while operating the social media. Most of the social network sites, makes the users sign an agreement that will allow the site to use the material that they post on the site (Debatin, 2011). Moreover, anything they post on the Internet never dies and can be copied, distributed and repurposed without their knowledge. So, a privacy literate user should always consider a temporal privacy protection while sharing any post, picture, comment or location to limit the free-floating information and its possible abuse in the future.
*   6\. Be cautious of unverified or unnecessary links: The attackers can install malicious software, collect personal information or launch phishing attack by trapping the user into clicking random links (Shahriar & Devendran, 2014). Thus, users of the social networking sites are advised not to click on any links posted by third party applications or from friends without verifying its validity.
*   7\. Avoid the use of smartphones for posting updates on social networking sites: The digital integration of social and user activity data makes mobile social networks an interesting context to examine privacy. The use of mobile applications for social networking sites is increasingly being used due to their always connected and always carried around nature (Stroud, 2008). But, configuring the privacy on the mobile devices is complex as compared to the desktop devices as they can reveal precise and real time information about the user location and preferences. This real time information spread is the privacy breach and can lead to new challenges and opportunities for social networking services and the users.
*   8\. Be cautious about the check-in feature: Most of the social networking sites allow the users to check-in their geographical location. But users should concern about broadcasting their location information through check-in as people will now know who they are, their address, their current location and where they are not. This information can easily be used against them by the criminals and malicious users. Thus, social media users are advised to turn off the location services for the social media to protect their location data and cybercasting.
*   9\. Be considerate: A responsible user will consider the privacy of others and should not post the information about other users without their permission. So, if a user has to share a post, picture or memory with their friend, they should always consider asking them before posting it. A perceptive user can also adjust their privacy settings to control the tagging and posting on their wall by other users.
*   10\. Trim your friend list: A perceptive user should frequently perform a health check on their friend list not only to limit who sees their activity, but also to trace careless friends who can leak their private data to third parties as happened with Cambridge Analytica (Isaak & Hanna, 2018).
*   11\. Be suspicious: Like email phishing attacks, cyber attacker can target the trust feature of social networks to trick the users into social media phishing. A common attack method is hacking into their friends account or pretend to be their friend to steal their data or wealth (Krombholz et al., 2015). So, users of social media are advised to be careful while connecting and disclosing any private or financial information with anyone.

Technical Suggestions

The proliferation of smart device, their usage and capability along with the popularity of social networking sites raise serious concerns for the privacy protection of technically weak users. Thus, along with the privacy literation, a user should also be aware of the technical capabilities and loopholes of the devices, applications, public networks and social networking sites. The technical literacy will provide the spatial access barriers to the user’s personal and sensitive information. Every social networking user should follow the below mentioned guidelines to protect their information:

*   1\. Adjust account privacy setting: The privacy settings of social networking sites allow the user to customize their account to control what to share and with whom. Thus, a perceptive user should carefully investigate the privacy settings of the social media account to better protect their privacy. Most of the social networking sites will allow the user to control the following: 
    *   a. Visibility of their post and data
    *   b. How people will find the user and who can post on his/her wall or tag him/her
    *   c. Third party applications that are allowed to access and interact with their profile
    *   d. Ability to remove their profile from being found when someone looks for them on a search engine.
    *   e. Control targeted advertising
    *   f. Control linkage to other social networking sites
    *   g. Switch off location services
    *   h. Switch off facial recognition feature
*   2\. Device privacy settings: The increased usage of mobile social networking applications presents huge challenges for protecting the privacy and security of users (Sadeh et al., 2009). The lost and stolen devices along with the insufficient security measures and privacy settings will further complicate the problem. Thus, a diligent user should consider the following to ensure their privacy on the mobile devices: 
    *   a. Use a password, fingerprint or a facial recognition feature to lock the mobile device and prevent unauthorized access to the social media application.
    *   b. Turn off location sharing.
    *   c. Switch off synchronization between apps
    *   d. Always read the privacy policy and access request to the phone and camera by different applications
    *   e. Accountability and accessibility for third-party opt-in
*   3\. Selective use of third-party applications: Most of the games and third-party applications available on the social networking sites will require access to the user’s social media account. Moreover, the hackers are increasingly using attractive applications to target the potential victims and gain access to their account or to collect their personal information (Rahman et al., 2015). So, users are advised to carefully investigate and minimize the use of third-party applications. The investigation should involve checking the ratings, review and number of downloads before they actually install it. The existing users are also motivated to review the applications that are currently accessing your profile and revoke access to unused and untrusted applications.
*   4\. Install security software: Establishment of privacy settings is essential but not sufficient means to protect the privacy of the social networking user. Thus, using the up-to date security software, web browser, operating system and social media application along with the sufficient privacy settings will provide the best defense against the newest known security and privacy threats.
*   5\. Always read the privacy policy and stay updated on privacy policy changes: The privacy policy will explain how the social networking site can collect and use the information of its customers. A diligent user should always read and regularly watch for the updates to the privacy policy. The following points need to be considered, while reviewing the privacy policy: 
    *   a. The privacy policies can change dramatically over time.
    *   b. The terms of service may have the important information as well. So, consider reviewing it in detail.
    *   c. The privacy policy will not cover the third-party applications and their interactions with the social networks. Turn off location sharing.
*   6\. Use of privacy-enhancing technologies: A diligent user can use the privacy-enhancing technologies to protect their privacy. These privacy-enhancing technologies are sticky policies, use of private browsing, Data track tool, communication anonymizers and selective disclosure technologies (Fischer-Hübner & Berthold, 2017). 
    *   a. Sticky policies are used to technically enforce preferences when personal data is shared across multiple parties.
    *   b. The use of private browsing will protect privacy by not tracking the digital footprint of users.
    *   c. Data track will record the history of all online transactions, to check which personal information has been disclosed to whom.
    *   d. Communication anonymizers are used to protect the users from web tracking.
    *   e. Selective disclosure technologies are used to limit the type or quantity of information disclosed to third-parties. The privacy policies can change dramatically over time.

Suggestions for the Social Network Platform

The social networking sites are penalized for the privacy violation in the form of reputation harm, cost of non-compliance and loss of user trust. Thus, the future of the social networking platform will depend on the steps and countermeasures they are taking to protect the privacy and safety of their users. These steps may be the technical or administrative steps taken by the social network designers to ensure the proper handling of private information or to prevent the activities that pose privacy risk. The owners of the social networking sites should take the following measures to minimize the risk of repeating the past privacy scandals and to safeguard the future.

Technical Security

Considering the power and sensitivity of data being shared through social networking sites, the designers should carefully assess the limitations and flaws of the social network design and take appropriate measures to protect against the potential attacks. Some of the serious flaws that compromise the privacy of the users and need to be dealt with are as follows:

*   1\. Validation of user credential during registration process: The lack of an adequate validation method during the new user registration leads to the proliferation of fake accounts on the social networking site (Adewole et al., 2017). Thus, social network designers need to design a new mechanism to validate the user credentials during the registration process.
*   2\. Validation of information shared on the social media: The social networking sites are becoming a novel platform for information sharing with a large audience without verifying the credibility of this information. Most of the social networking sites were not acting rigorously to control political misinformation and disinformation. However, the Facebook, Twitter and Instagram’s recent efforts to limit the spread of misinformation regarding coronavirus along with their educational pop-up with credible information from local health authorities and WHO website is appreciable (Hutchinson, 2020).
*   3\. Limit the information disclosed by the user status: The messenger programs used by many social networking sites provide the information about the availability of the users, whether or not they are currently using the service (Baccarella et al., 2018). The unusual patterns of user availability or information about user’s unavailability can be exploited by the malicious users. Thus, every social networking site needs to provide the user controls to limit the information being disclosed about the user’s online activity.
*   4\. Privacy by design: The privacy invasive nature of social networks calls for more transparent, structured and controlled platform for every individual user to meet their social and privacy needs. The existing social networking sites have to completely deconstruct and analyses their system by performing a privacy audit on their systems to identify weak points and create new user-friendly solutions. As the privacy by design principles are important for the design and operation of social networks (Islam & Iannella, 2011). Thus, below mentioned principles needs to be followed for managing the user privacy effectively and transparently: 
    *   a. Privacy as the default ensures that the users need not to take steps to secure their privacy rather the social networking system will automatically protect their data by following opt-in practices for the privacy settings. The need of this feature is evident from the fact that most of the users currently stick with the default, operator-chosen settings.
    *   b. Lifecycle protection principle considers the security of private information from the start to end. This means that information should enter securely in the system, retained safely and then destroyed properly.
    *   c. Accountability, openness and compliance are the basic feature of an effective and trusted system. Thus, the social networking sites need to be clear about the level of privacy it provides along with the accountability to the services provided through their platform including third-party services, information and external links.
    *   d. Respect for user privacy states that ensuring the privacy of the users should be the number concern of social networking sites. Thus, the social networking sites are optimized for users and their needs.
    *   e. Proactive not reactive principle states that the privacy breaches should be predicted and prevented before they actually happen. The social networking sites should provide the proactive privacy protection feature along with educating the users about the privacy issues.
    *   f. Privacy embedded into design states that the privacy should be embedded in design and should not diminish the functionality of the social networks.
    *   g. Full functionality ensures that trade-offs should not be made to accommodate either privacy or functionality. So, a trusted social networking platform should safeguard against unwanted correlation of user activities and real-time spread of information. The privacy policies can change dramatically over time.
*   5\. Use of privacy enhancing technologies: The privacy enhancing technologies are based on the idea of shaping technology according to the privacy principles of data minimization, anonymization and pseudonymization (Seničar et al., 2003). 
    *   a. The objective of the data minimization is to minimize the amount of personal data collected and used by the service provider.
    *   b. The objective of the anonymization is to maximize the privacy while minimizing the information loss in the released data. This process will reduce the risk of re-identification.
    *   c. Pseudonymizing is the processing of personal data in a way that the data can no longer be attributed to a specific data subject without using additional information. The privacy policies can change dramatically over time.
*   6\. Use of transparency enhancing technologies: A wide variety of tools are available to enhance the transparency and awareness of users. These tools are icons (Holtz et al., 2011), privacy nudges (Wang et al., 2013) and privacy dashboards (Talukder et al., 2010). The social networking platforms can utilize these tools for the notification and better understanding of users.

Administrative Control

The administrative control refers to the change in the behavior of the social networking site owners to better protect the privacy of their users and to gain and sustain a good reputation among its users. These administrative controls emphasize on the open and fair information practices. A trusted social networking site should follow the following practices to provide a safe and trustworthy environment to its users:

*   1\. Transparent privacy policies, terms and conditions: The General data protection regulation (GDPR) mandates the user consent in order to collect, store and process personal data (Hoofnagle et al., 2019). But, in order to consent to something, user first needs to understand it. Most of the social networking sites are publishing their privacy policy in the technical and legal terms that is not understandable to the general public. Thus, a trustworthy social networking site should provide a transparent privacy policy by clearly defining what data they will collect, how they will use, store and share it and for what duration.
*   2\. Limit the disclosure of navigation data: The social networking sites are actively collecting a large amount of data varying from minor details such as user’s mouse movement to the data about their online and offline actions along with details of purchases from third party service providers. A trustworthy social networking site should only collect the limited amount of data with a specific purpose for which the user’s consent has been received.
*   3\. Informed changes: A trusted social networking site should always inform its users about the new features or any changes in the privacy policy and terms of use.
*   4\. Default activation of privacy controls: In a world, where only a fraction of users changes software preferences or default settings, strict privacy controls should be activated by default. Social networking sites have to make a tough choice here as their business model is based on the open network that can engage its users and motivate extended browsing sessions. But, to ensure the privacy of the users and trustworthiness of the platform, social network site owners must provide strict privacy settings as a default setting.
*   5\. Better restrictions on the third-party applications: The social network site owners should ensure that the third-party applications comply with their user’s privacy policy. This requirement can be fulfilled by incorporating privacy at the system design level by restricting the direct access of the third-party applications to the user data. They can do their business by providing user information through the carefully designed interfaces that follow the principle of anonymity. Adrienne and David (2008) have proposed a Privacy-by-Proxy technique to protect the privacy by limiting the data access to the third-party applications. However, its requirement to reveal the business strategy to the social networking site averts the third-party applications.
*   6\. Risk announcement: The social networking sites can do a great service to its users by announcing the dangers of security breaches and outside monitoring to the public profiles or every time users share information with public or large audience. This will educate the users about the risks associated with participating in the social media and consequences of their actions.
*   7\. Compliance with the regulation and frameworks: The social networking sites should comply with the legal obligations under the GDPR (Hoofnagle et al., 2019) while storing and processing the user data. This compliance will keep the data protected by minimization the risk of data leak and supporting the transparency and accountability requirements.

DISCUSSION

The above sections have discussed the privacy issues of social networks and highlighted the importance of active participation of users and social network owners to protect the privacy. We have provided taxonomy to identify the problematic activities and to aid the understanding of the privacy threats in the online social networks. This research demonstrates that the lack of self-control and privacy literacy of users, business orientation and inherent design flaws of social networking sites (Hatfield, 2018) fuel the invader’s attack strategy to acquire the sensitive information about the users and society. The ease of information access (tracking) or data gathering (aggregation) without the user knowledge along with the data mishandling (insecurity), its use for unintended purposes (data processing) and the diffusion of private facts on the social networks further complicates the privacy problem. The existing literature has blamed the concept of social networking sites for increased privacy problems, as it facilitates the collection, processing and dissemination of information (Houghton et al., 2010). But we emphasize on the fact that the privacy problems are not caused by the social networking platform alone, but primarily through the activities of its users and owners. The main findings of our research are:

*   • Most of the privacy problems are the result of the careless and irresponsible user behavior as majority of the users lack the general awareness about the privacy risk, privacy policies and privacy settings. This can be addressed by creating awareness and understanding of privacy problems so that users can implement appropriate privacy controls and balance privacy consideration against their social interest. This chapter will aid the user understanding by providing the detailed analysis of the privacy problems from social engineering perspective and easy to follow instructions to address them.
*   • To gain a positive reputation, the social networking sites needs to respect the user privacy by providing a safer and trustworthy social platform. This can be achieved by following the GDPR and principles of open information practices by fostering the opt-in practices for the privacy settings along with the appropriate measures to address the limitations and flaws of social network design.
*   • To better aid the understanding of privacy threats and implementation of privacy control, identification of threat actors whose intentional or unintentional harmful activities compromises the privacy of users is required. FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS

The scale of the social networking sites coupled with an increased scrutiny has pressurized the owners of social media to provide the increased level of user privacy. Despite these measures, the privacy threats exist and significant efforts are needed to protect the privacy of users and society as a whole. This section will propose some promising research directions to pave the way for potential privacy protection methods.

*   • Privacy Preservation Techniques: The popularity of social networks has made it possible to create a large amount of data about users, their interests and relationships. The social network service providers are compelled to publish their data to better understand the sociological and behavioral aspects of individuals and groups. The presence of potentially sensitive information in the dataset mandates the sanitization of this data before the release. The reported attacks on the published data prove the practicality of the re-identification and disclosure attack (Li et al., 2017; Qian et al., 2017; Li, 2019). Thus, significant research efforts are needed to ensure the privacy in the published data and to simplify the complexity of the process for data publishers.
*   • Decentralized Architecture: The centralized architecture of social networks is prone to privacy violations as the social network providers retain the full control of user data, including private messages and browsing history. Thus, significant research efforts are needed for the decentralization of data and services to transfer the control from the provider to the social network user.
*   • Risk Assessment and Solutions: As the social login is one of the attractive features for the login of different website and applications, the social networks work as a web tracker (Kayes & Iamnitchi, 2017). So, future research work can explore a comprehensive risk assessment and solutions that consider social networks as potential trackers.
*   • Privacy policies with an automated compliance assurance function: A trusted social networking site should have an open and transparent privacy handling practices by clearly specifying ‘who’ will access the user’s information, ‘how’ it will be accessed and ‘where’ it will be accessed in social networks. The automated compliance assurance function should serve as a “safety net” to identify, capture emerging privacy risks and take appropriate measures to handle complaints and suspicious activities.
*   • Proactive and automated communication techniques on risk: A trusted social networking site should proactively inform the users about the potential privacy risks and provide easy to access options for reporting the privacy invasions. To implement this, an automated communication technique will be needed, that can track the user activity and inform them about the possible consequences of their actions.

CONCLUSION

The proliferation of smartphones and other mobile devices along with the widespread internet access enable the social networking sites to track every individual user’s precise location, behavior, political orientation, purchase patterns, email and SMS communication patterns, social contacts and even the biometrics. These data collection practices raise problematic privacy issues as the social networking sites are misusing this information to pollute the digital information ecosystem and try to shape each aspect of the public life. The identification of privacy threats is an important task, as it will educate the users about the enlightened understanding of the social networks and its unforeseen consequences. It will guide the users about the ways in which privacy can be violated and motivate them to be attentive about the potential offending activity before publishing their personal detail. This chapter has provided a detailed understanding of the value of personal data, threats it is exposed to and easy to incorporate suggestions to maintain the desired level of privacy. The key findings of this research are:

*   • Majority of the privacy threats are arising from the careless and imprudent behavior of social network users (Heravi et al., 2018). Thus, this research suggests achieving the required level of privacy will require much effort from every individual social media user. To mitigate the privacy breaches, the users should be privacy literate and their online interactions should follow the principles of healthy interpersonal relations of the offline world.
*   • The inherent design flaws, and business orientation of social networking platforms results in the violation of privacy rights of its users. Thus, social networking platforms are encouraged to follow the open and fair information practices to ensure the user privacy by providing a safe and trustworthy environment.

In short, we can conclude that the privacy preservation is the joint responsibility of social network owners, individual users, and the regulatory bodies. The privacy preservation in the digital world will require more than passing laws and ordinary compliance to data privacy regulations. Thus, universal ethical behavior and adherence to the healthy interpersonal relations by the users and owners of the social media will reduce the privacy violation incidents and provide a reliable platform for socializing, public deliberation and democracy.

KEY TERMS AND DEFINITIONS

Appropriation Attack: The use of social networks to disseminate certain information about a person or organization to benefit the aim and interests of others.

Cyber-Espionage: The use of social media by state sponsored cyber groups for the theft of the confidential information such as technical innovation or military plans.

Cyber-Vetting: Acquisition and use of online information about the target individual from online sources to investigate about their reputation and behavior.

Distortion: Intentional modification or manipulation of the content or content display to damage reputation, to perform scam or to avoid censorship.

Information Diffusion: The process of spreading information or knowledge to individuals or group of individuals thorough interactions.

Invasion: The use of social networking sites to intrude into the user’s domain. This may include monitoring, tracking, profiling, or identity theft.

Privacy Nudges: The use of choice architecture to protect user’s privacy by altering user’s behavior in a predictable way without forbidding any options.
